subject: Inference impact settlement - Horizon Labs
messages:
From: Anya Patel <anya@horizon-labs.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: procurements@horizon-labs.com, devops@horizon-labs.com
Date: Fri, 09 Jul 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Inference cluster incident — request for remedial settlement

Hi Irene,

Thanks again for the post-incident update. To recap on our side: on 2027-07-08 between ~02:14-02:47 UTC (our peak batch window) we saw elevated 95th/99th tail latency and ~4% failed requests across three inference endpoints that drive our real-time scoring pipeline. That spike caused several downstream job retries and a visible customer impact for two hours.

Our procurement team has asked us to open a formal request for an SLA adjustment/settlement. Can you confirm Horizon Labs’ eligibility for a service credit, the calculation methodology you will apply, and an expected timeline for a proposed credit and issuance? We need a number to present to our finance team by next week.

I attached a short incident summary from our ops team (horizon_incident_summary.pdf). Happy to hop on a quick call if that helps.

Thanks,
Anya Patel
Head of ML Platform
Horizon Labs

Attachment: horizon_incident_summary.pdf
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Anya Patel <anya@horizon-labs.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 09 Jul 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Inference cluster incident — request for remedial settlement

Hi Anya —

Thanks for the summary and the attachment. I'm sorry again for the disruption. We will validate eligibility and produce a transparent calculation for Horizon Labs. Next steps from our side:

- Internal verification (Marissa): confirm outage window(s) and affected capacity slices.
- Billing calc (Ben): map downtime to the SLA terms and compute the credit against July invoice.
- External-facing summary (me): confirm the proposed credit, provide a short breakdown, and list issuance steps (credit note vs invoice adjustment).

I expect we can share a preliminary number by EOW (working to accelerate). Please confirm the account/project id you want the credit applied to and whether we should route the formal credit note to procurements@horizon-labs.com.

For transparency, I'm attaching our SLA settlement process doc so you know how we calculate offsets.

Irene Choi
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
irene_choi@redwood.com

Attachment: redwood_sla_process.pdf
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 10 Jul 2027 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Inference cluster incident — preliminary eligibility check

Irene / Ben —

I pulled the serving logs and router traces for Horizon Labs (customer id HL-8923). Quick notes:
- Incident window (observed by runtime): 2027-07-08 02:12:40–02:47:10 UTC.
- Affected shards: pool-a (2/8 replicas) and pool-b (1/6 replicas) suffering transient OOM/eviction behavior coincident with a degraded kernel rollout.
- Estimated request failures: ~4.1% of calls during the window; latency p95 jumped from 210ms -> 1,350ms.

Per the SLA (monthly uptime), we treat this as partial degradation that meets the "reliability" clause for service redress. Proposed approach for a first-pass calc: compute the proportional credit based on the percentage of requests impacted during the incident window relative to monthly billable request volume, then cap by the SLA credit slab.

Ben — can you produce a draft credit table using HL's July forecasted consumption and the above impact figures? I'll attach the runtime slices we used to validate.

Marissa
Sr. Reliability Operations
Redwood Inference

> On Fri, Jul 9, 2027 at 2:05 PM Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com> wrote:
> 
> > Thanks for the summary and the attachment. I'm sorry again for the disruption...
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Jul 2027 11:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Inference cluster incident — draft credit calculation attached

Team —

Attached is a draft calculation (Horizon_Credit_Calc_v1.xlsx). Summary:
- Baseline: Horizon Labs monthly invoice forecast (July): $267,500 (compute + embeddings).
- Incident-adjusted impacted request share: 4.1% across the window; mapped to 0.67% of the monthly bill by weighting for the window length and expected request distribution.
- Preliminary credit: $17,925 (rounded to nearest $25). This falls within the SLA credit cap for a single incident.

Notes and ask:
- I used the forecasted consumption HubSpot record HL-8923 and the runtime slices Marissa provided. If you want to apply a different denominator (actual billable usage vs forecast), I can re-run.
- If approved, I will open a billing adjustment and create the credit note; we typically apply to the next invoice cycle and notify procurement.

Approving signatures: Irene or finance lead.

Ben Carter
Billing Lead, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

Attachment: Horizon_Credit_Calc_v1.xlsx
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Anya Patel <anya@horizon-labs.com>, procurements@horizon-labs.com
Date: Tue, 13 Jul 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Inference cluster incident — approval and issuance plan

Ben / Marissa —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. I approve the proposed credit of $17,925 as outlined in Ben's calc. Ben, please proceed with the billing adjustment and issue a formal credit note to procurements@horizon-labs.com with a copy to Anya. Use the following issuance instructions:

- Reference: HL-8923 / HubSpot ticket HL-8923.
- Apply credit to July invoice; if invoice already settled, issue a credit note to be applied against the next cycle.
- Notify me once the credit note is posted and add an entry to the issuance_tracker.csv (please attach link).

Anya — we will process the credit and you should see the credit note delivered within 3 business days; posting may take up to one invoice cycle. Apologies again for the impact — we are adding an extra canary step to kernel rollouts to reduce recurrence.

Irene Choi
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
irene_choi@redwood.com
